findings.title: Concurrent-reader test does not join the reader thread, making it racy and ineffective
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the background reader thread is started but never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll=true and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty, so the test can pass while the reader thread is still mid-request or has not yet had a chance to hit the deleted-group window; any exception thrown after the assertion (or on the final iteration) is silently lost. The reader loop may also loop zero times if the deletes finish before the thread schedules, in which case the test exercises nothing. The test should join the thread (e.g., set a done flag, interrupt/join, then assert) to reliably reproduce the race it is meant to cover.

findings.title: LazyModel supplier caches a previously-resolved delegate, so a later concurrent delete still returns a stale model
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount now guards against modelSupplier.get() returning null, but modelSupplier is a LazyModel that caches the delegate once resolved. If the underlying group was already resolved through this adapter (e.g., via getSubGroupsStream(search, ...) at lines 254-268, which use the same supplier) and is then deleted by another thread, modelSupplier.get() returns the cached non-null GroupModel and getSubGroupsCount() is invoked on a deleted group, which can still fail. The null guard only covers the case where the model was never resolved before the delete; the fix is incomplete for repeated access through the same cached adapter.

findings.title: populateSubGroupCount can now propagate a null subGroupCount into GroupRepresentation
findings.body: With GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() changed to return null when the group has been concurrently deleted, GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount stores that null via representation.setSubGroupCount(null). Consumers that unbox getSubGroupCount() (the representation field is Long, and Admin UI / REST clients commonly treat it as a required count when populateSubGroupCount is requested) will see the field disappear from the JSON or risk NullPointerException on unboxing. Either the deleted-group case should be skipped (not emit/merge the representation) or the null contract should be documented and handled at this call site, rather than silently producing a representation with a missing subgroup count.
